co_other_critters.blurb: A small bolted wall tucked into Clear Creek Canyon near Tunnel 5, in the Golden foothills west of Denver. Twenty-two of its 25 climbs are sport routes, joined by two trad lines and one top-rope. Difficulty runs wide but leans friendly: most routes sit between 5.6 and 5.10, with a handful of harder lines up to the low 5.13 range. That makes it a reasonable pick for newer leaders building mileage alongside stronger partners. The rock is gneiss, and the wall faces south, so it collects plenty of sun. Expect warm climbing on cool days and a toasty time in summer. Most routes are single pitch, and the canyon road keeps the drive short from the Front Range.

co_left_side_of_the_river.blurb: A cluster of forested boulders beside the North St. Vrain in Wild Basin, the quieter southern corner of Rocky Mountain National Park near Estes Park. About 25 problems here, all bouldering, spread over several boulders such as Dating Jesus, Bankhead and The Open Road. Grades cover nearly the whole range, from V1 up to V10, with the bulk of the problems in the V5 to V9 band, so it suits strong boulderers more than beginners. The setting is shaded woodland at moderate elevation rather than alpine, and most boulders sit close to the trail or a short step off it. Bring pads and plan on a walk in through the trees.

co_raven_the.blurb: One of the more convenient crags in Staunton State Park, in the foothills southwest of Denver. The Raven holds about 25 routes: nineteen sport, five trad and a single top-rope. Grades start around 5.6 and climb steadily, with a good cluster of 5.7 to 5.9 lines for moderate climbers and a solid group of 5.11 to 5.13 test pieces for stronger ones, plus a lone 5.14. The crag sits on the east side of the park, reached from the meadow lot, and the rock is featured. Single-pitch outings with a mix of bolts and gear make it a flexible half-day choice.

co_us_highway_550.blurb: A string of frozen waterfalls along the road that climbs south from Ouray toward Red Mountain Pass. Twenty-five ice lines are recorded here, nearly all of them WI4, with a few WI5s and one WI3, so this is mostly an intermediate-to-advanced venue. A few mixed pitches turn up as well. Many lines are visible from the roadside and the walk to the base is generally short, which makes for quick days, though several are multi-pitch and some sit under big snow bowls. Avalanche hazard after heavy snowfall is a real consideration, and ice quality changes a lot from one winter to the next.

co_chicken_head_ranch.blurb: A freestanding formation on the lower west side of Devil's Head in the South Platte region, southwest of Denver. Climbing wraps around all four sides, so you can follow the sun or hide from it. About 25 routes, mostly sport (21) with four trad lines. The grade spread is broad, from a couple of 5.6s through a middle band of 5.8 to 5.10, then a strong run of 5.11 and 5.12 with one 5.13 for the hard-hitters. Popular lines include easy to moderate classics as well as a few steep, sustained leads. Expect a hike of roughly half an hour from the trailhead, uphill over a pass.

co_oceanic_wall.blurb: A granite wall at the north end of Upper Dream Canyon, west of Boulder, sitting almost at creek level with small cobble beaches nearby. Of its 25 climbs, nineteen are sport, five trad and one is a boulder problem. Grades start near 5.8 and run to 5.13, with the bulk landing between 5.9 and 5.12, so it rewards climbers with some experience. Most routes are one or two pitches, many are bolted, and older bolts and anchors were replaced on numerous lines. The setting is a creekside canyon with a quiet feel. Spring through early fall is the comfortable window.

co_brown_wall_the.blurb: A sunny crag in the Thunder Ridge zone of the South Platte, west of Denver and Colorado Springs, and the place where climbing at the ridge got started. Trad dominates: nineteen of 25 routes are gear-protected, with five sport lines and a top-rope. The rock has a rough, textured surface. Difficulty skews hard, with most routes between 5.10 and 5.12 and a few at 5.13 and 5.14, plus a single easy line, so this is an area for confident leaders. Crack and flake climbing, along with face moves, sets the style. Reaching the base takes some effort, as the wall sits well back behind the lower canyons.

co_bob_s_rock.blurb: A roadside granite wall just north of Buena Vista, close to the Arkansas River corridor, with vertical to overhanging rock around 75 feet tall. The stone is crystalline and has a feel similar to Boulder Canyon granite. The 25 routes split evenly between sport and trad, with one top-rope. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.13, but the sweet spot is 5.9 through 5.12, so intermediate and strong climbers will find the most to do. A few quickdraws and a small rack cover most lines. Short walk-ins, fun moves and nearby camping make it a popular local stop alongside neighboring crags like Turtle Rock.

_conflicts.co_brown_wall_the: Stored rock is granite; https://app.advcollective.com/climbing/dragonfly-at-the-brown-wall-a-classic-trad-climb-on-thunder-ridge calls it brown sandstone, while https://www.mountainproject.com/area/106125945/the-brown-wall does not name the rock. Left unchanged.
